editorial.headline: The National Opening—and Bali Stop Sign—for Bakery Wholesalers
editorial.standfirst: Wholesale trading in bread, cakes and other bakery products is nationally open to foreign investment, but Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks registration for this activity.
editorial.body:
This activity is the wholesale trade of bread, cakes and other bakery products: the commercial distribution layer that moves bakery goods through the market rather than their production. Nationally, it is classified as open to foreign investment, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. That is the starting point, and it is an important one: the national position is not a partial opening or a foreign-share cap, but a fully open ceiling under the cited presidential regulations.

The activity is open across the stated business scales—Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. In practical terms, the classification accommodates wholesale bakery-product businesses at each of those registered scales. The scope remains specific, however: bread, cakes and other bakery products are the goods at its centre. A sound registration narrative should keep that commercial focus clear, because the code’s definition is framed around wholesale trade in those products.

For a foreign-owned company considering Bali, the national opening does not settle the question. Bali blocks PMA registration for this activity today. At the Besar scale, every listed scope is assessed in OSS as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah risk, placing the activity within Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. The block is therefore not a reduction of the national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling; it is a Bali-specific restriction on PMA registration.

That distinction deserves to be made without softening it. A foreign investor may see an activity that is nationally TERBUKA and assume Bali follows the same result. Here it does not. The Bali classification is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO, and the recorded basis is the low or medium-low OSS risk profile at the Besar scale together with the moratorium cited as taking effect in May 2026. For founders, the reliable reading is straightforward: national foreign-investment openness exists, yet Bali is not available for PMA registration of this activity under the stated provincial rule.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness and Bali eligibility are different questions: this activity is open nationally, but blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
